title: Your system design roadmap
idea: Your next step after low-level design (LLD) is high-level design (HLD): choosing the services, data stores and network calls your classes live inside.
points: You can now turn a vague prompt into tested, extensible Java classes.
Deepen LLD with full case studies that add a database schema and an API.
Then learn HLD: how services, caches, queues and data stores fit together.
Keep one timed practice problem a week so the method stays automatic.

hero.title: Where to go after this book

edges.label: practise
edges.caption: Turn the book into habit: one graded problem a week, against a 45-minute clock.

edges.label: go deeper
edges.caption: The LLD Case Studies book takes each design on to a database schema, an API and a frontend.

edges.label: broaden
edges.caption: Backend Engineering covers HTTP, databases and deployment: the ground HLD stands on.

edges.label: zoom out
edges.caption: A case study's API and schema become one box in a larger HLD diagram.

edges.label: scale
edges.caption: HLD chooses services and data stores, and how caching, sharding and queues connect them.

edges.label: apply
edges.caption: Use the same method at work: write use cases, sketch classes, then code and review.

edges.label: combine
edges.caption: Senior design work mixes both: HLD for the system, LLD inside each service.

takeaway: Design the classes well, then learn the system around them.
